description:
Found during fz-kdt.34.5: `demand_on_stall` reached ZERO handlers on HEAD.
The emit passes `&u64 producer_pokes` (drive.rs stall pass); the JSONL attach
was typed `attach_raw_event2::<usize, HashSet<FactKey>, _>`. Bus dispatch is
runtime type-matched with silent fall-through (`bus.rs`: downcast miss ->
`else { return; }`), so the mismatch compiled clean and the event silently
vanished -- for as long as the handler existed. Nobody noticed because absence
is invisible.

This is the same hazard class fz-kdt.34.4 documented for arity changes, now
proven live for TYPE drift on an existing handler. Every
`attach_raw_event*`/`attach_raw_span*` registration is one refactor away from
going dead with no compile error and no test failure.

## Deliver

Force agreement between emit sites and attachments so drift is a hard failure,
not a silent drop. Candidate shapes (pick after research, prefer
correct-by-construction over an audit):

- Shared payload type aliases or a typed event-name registry: the name and its
  payload tuple declared ONCE, both emit and attach reference it (drift = type
  error).
- Failing that: a coverage test that drives one real compile with a counting
  handler per registered raw attachment and asserts every attachment matched
  at least one event whose name it registered for (catches dead-on-every-
  compile handlers like this one; document the events a trivial compile
  genuinely never fires and probe them individually).
- One-off audit of all current registrations against their emit sites is the
  floor, not the fix -- record findings here if done first.

fz-kdt.34.5 fixed the one known instance (retyped to u64) and its TDD-3 test
now pins demand_on_stall content publicly, so THIS event cannot silently die
again. The others remain unguarded.
title: Silently-dead typed handlers: force emit/attach type agreement
